reason: The sources provide strong multi-source corroboration across independent sites for all major aspects of the Artemis II mission and its record-setting flight.
story: More than half a century after Apollo 17 departed the lunar surface in 1972, humanity finally ventured beyond low Earth orbit with Artemis II. In April 2026, NASA launched four astronauts—commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, and mission specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen—aboard the Orion spacecraft Integrity, propelled by the colossal Space Launch System rocket from Florida's Kennedy Space Center. Over a ten-day flight, Orion looped around the far side of the Moon on a safe free-return trajectory powered by ESA's European Service Module. Rather than orbiting or landing, the mission served as the ultimate trial run for future surface landings. In doing so, the crew smashed Apollo 13's historic distance record, reaching 252,756 miles from Earth—farther into the cosmos than any human in history. The mission carried the first woman, the first person of color, and the first non-American into deep space, concluding with a Pacific Ocean splashdown.
angle: During their lunar flyby, the Artemis II crew shattered Apollo 13's half-century-old record, traveling 252,756 miles from Earth to become the farthest humans from home in history.

claims.claim: Artemis II was the first crewed mission to travel beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972.
The mission was the first flight of NASA's Space Launch System rocket with astronauts aboard.
Artemis II marked the first crewed flight of NASA's Orion spacecraft.
The four-person crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
Reid Wiseman served as mission commander and Victor Glover served as pilot.
Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen served as mission specialists on the flight.
Jeremy Hansen was selected by the Canadian Space Agency, becoming the first non-American to fly to the vicinity of the Moon.
Christina Koch became the first woman to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
Victor Glover became the first Black astronaut to fly around the Moon.
The crew named their Orion capsule Integrity.
Artemis II launched in April 2026 from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
The spacecraft reached a maximum distance from Earth of 252,756 miles (406,771 kilometers).
Artemis II broke Apollo 13's record for the farthest distance humans have traveled from Earth.
The Orion spacecraft flew on a lunar free-return trajectory without orbiting or landing on the Moon.
Orion was powered and propelled in deep space by ESA's European Service Module.
The crew performed manual proximity operations in Earth orbit using the SLS upper stage as a target.
Artemis II concluded with a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The mission was an approximately 10-day test flight to validate spacecraft systems ahead of future crewed lunar landings.

disputed: Closest lunar approach distance: S1 and S6 report the flyby altitude as 4,067 to 4,070 miles above the lunar surface, whereas early preflight reports in S4 anticipated a closest approach of 6,479 miles; scripts should attribute early numbers to preflight projections or focus on the confirmed distance from Earth.

Reentry profile: S1 details that NASA replaced a planned skip reentry with a steeper direct descent to minimize heat shield exposure following Artemis I erosion, while earlier documentation referenced a skip reentry; scripts should attribute the trajectory adjustment to post-Artemis I heat shield findings.
